summary: Specializing in Indology and computational studies, Jan Christian Schaffert studied at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, where he was also attested in 2026 as a project collaborator on EdiKILex.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan Fontein worked in art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin and served as curator at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht University under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (PhD 1929) and at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and the Indology post (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He was a professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).
Jan Jaworski worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (1922–1928) and under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

Jan N. Bremmer is a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, later serving as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Groningen (1990; 1996–2005).

Jan Nattier is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held faculty posts at Indiana University Bloomington (1992–2005) and Soka University (2004–2010).

Jan P. Hogendijk is a historian of mathematics and Indologist who earned his doctorate from Utrecht University in 1983. He served as professor of the history of mathematics at Leiden University (2004–2009) and Utrecht University (2005).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper. He also studied under several traditional teachers, including Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Van Bragt was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at KU Leuven. He served as director (~1976–1991) and later professor emeritus (~1998–2007) at Nanzan University.

Jan Westerhoff is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned PhDs from the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and from SOAS, and was appointed Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford in ~2014.

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University. He served as Chair at Leiden (1950–1956) and department head at the Australian National University (1965–1986).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under David P. Jackson and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held posts at the University of Hamburg, the University of Munich, and the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006).
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of London in 1969 under the supervision of Nathaniel Tarn and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at the University of Leeds and is attested as a research fellow at the University of Manchester in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religion. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College under Robert Alexander Neil, and later held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1898–1922).
Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who held posts at Cornell University, serving as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religion who earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. She taught at Amherst College (1987–2001) before becoming Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard Divinity School in 2001.
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances Wilson.
